title: Black Tentacles
notes: The Black Tentacles mission is the unchanged feature contract; this plan only binds it to the review workflow. All 36 acceptance identifiers (BT01-BT36) remain in force. Engine-behavior claims require native observations; agreement between the developer and reviewer cannot establish engine behavior. Distinguish 'mechanically complete', 'ready for visual review' and 'released' exactly as the mission's Section 12 defines them. The focused-validation policy, guarded push path, runtime leases, disposable fixtures, immutable KMG_AUTOMATION_BASELINE and transactional restoration remain in force; the owner's normal-play installation is never modified.

checkpoints.scope: Mission Phases 0 and 1: verified native contracts and the decision record; the early moving field with one victim grab/release proof; a minimal area-owned check and a paid self-target escape command proven on a disposable fixture.
exit_conditions: Phase 0 exit evidence: a bounded design with verified Kingmaker 2.1.7b API names, a realistic persistence/scheduling approach, identity-collision search, and planning/BLACK-TENTACLES-DECISIONS.md covering the Section 5 adaptations, native seams and unresolved limits.

Phase 1 exit evidence: a candidate-bound in-game motion sample of the moving field and one grab/release, the chosen art route, and structured native observations that the area and action mechanisms behave as expected.
The design can support the remaining mission (Phases 2-4) without weakening any requirement; later-phase work is recorded as pending, not as a defect.
Runtime transactions restored the captured installation and saves.

checkpoints.scope: The complete mission (Phases 0-4) and the Section 12 handoff on one coherent draft-PR candidate.
exit_conditions: BT01-BT36 are each marked passed, failed, blocked or not run in planning/BLACK-TENTACLES-ACCEPTANCE.md, with evidence appropriate to each claim; required failures are not hidden among optional deferrals.
Native evidence supports ordinary spell access, both combat modes with pause, the paid Break Free escape, persistence across save/load, overlap, dismissal, cleanup and restoration claims.
Candidate-bound in-game motion and image samples are available for the owner's visual review (BT33-BT35); a static screenshot alone is insufficient.
Focused test/native results record scope, commands, durations and limits; evidence is tied to source and binary identity.
The handoff states separately whether the feature is mechanically complete and ready for visual review; it never claims release.
